## Table 1 — the field tower, as Bitcoin Script

Every module below is proven against `bsv.Script.Interpreter` under relay
policy flags at the BLS12-381 prime.

Two columns, because a module has two honest sizes and neither is *the* size.

**Standalone** is the module alone: it pushes the 381-bit prime itself, 49
bytes, which a locking script has to do once however many operations follow.

**Marginal** is the same module with the prime already supplied as a stack
value. For the small modules that is much smaller — `fp2.mul` is 39 rather
than 90, a difference larger than the module. For the large ones it is slightly
*larger*, and the reason is worth stating: a prime pushed by the module's own
prologue sits directly above its inputs, while one supplied beneath twenty-four
of them is deeper, and an `OP_PICK` past index 16 costs a byte more. Neither
column is a lower bound on the other; the depth of a constant is part of its
cost.

| module | operation | standalone | marginal | opcodes |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `fp2.mul` | Karatsuba, three Fp multiplications | 90 | 39 | 30 |
| `fp2.sqr` | two Fp multiplications | 77 | 22 | 22 |
| `fp2.add` | | 64 | 13 | 14 |
| `fp2.sub` | | 68 | 18 | 18 |
| `fp2.neg` | | 63 | 14 | 14 |
| `fp2.conj` | the Fp2 Frobenius, p ≡ 3 (mod 4) | 59 | 9 | 10 |
| `fp2.mulXi` | multiply by ξ = u + 1, no multiplications | 67 | 15 | 16 |
| `fp2.inv` | **witnessed**: a·a⁻¹ = 1, both bounds | 101 | 51 | 36 |
| `fp6.mul` | Karatsuba, six Fp2 multiplications | 756 | 721 | 520 |
| `fp12.mul` | Karatsuba, eighteen Fp2 multiplications | 3,073 | 3,110 | 2,036 |
| `fp12.sqr` | general squaring | 2,292 | 2,301 | 1,540 |
| `fp12.cycSqr` | Granger–Scott, cyclotomic subgroup only | 1,259 | 1,292 | 968 |
| `fp12.mulLine` | sparse: nine of twelve coefficients are zero | 2,051 | 2,018 | 1,310 |
| `fp12.frob` | f ↦ f^p, six conjugations and seven products | 715 | 675 | 330 |
| `fp12.inv` | **witnessed**: one Fp12 product and twelve bounds | 3,431 | 3,414 | 2,166 |
| `fp12.powX` | f ↦ f^\|x\|, MSB-first, 63 squarings and 5 products | 98,902 | 101,353 | 71,954 |
| `g2.stepDouble` | tangent at T, and 2T | 552 | 503 | 375 |
| `g2.stepAdd` | chord through T and Q, and T + Q | 535 | 487 | 363 |

**Cyclotomic squaring is 43.9% smaller than general squaring**, and the sparse line
product is 35.1% smaller than a general Fp12 product.

## Table 2 — the pairing

| stage | composition | bytes | opcodes | witnessed values |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Miller loop | 63 tangents, 5 chords, 68 line products, 63 squarings | 332,977 | 215,308 | 136 |
| final exponentiation | easy part, 5 ladders, 15 terms, 19 Frobenius maps | 592,008 | 411,505 | 12 |
| **e(P, Q)** | the two, chained | **935,334** | **627,013** | **148** |

The stages do not sum to the whole: chaining them costs
10,349 bytes that neither separate measurement contains.

## Table 3 — products of pairings share the accumulator

The squaring belongs to the *bit*, not to the line, so k pairings on one Miller
accumulator pay for 63 squarings between them and one final exponentiation.

| pairings | as a product | as separate pairings | saved |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 935,334 | 935,334 | — |
| 2 | 1,142,571 | 1,870,668 | 728,097 |
| 3 | 1,346,218 | 2,806,002 | 1,459,784 |

Each pairing after the first costs about 203,647 bytes rather than 935,334.

## Table 4 — a Groth16 verifier

e(A, B) · e(−L, γ) · e(−C, δ) = e(α, β), with 2 public inputs fixed at lock time.

| | |
| --- | ---: |
| locking script | 1,350,790 bytes |
| opcodes | 862,966 |
| witnessed values | 420 |
| chosen by the spender | Ax, Ay, Bx0, Bx1, By0, By1, Cx, Cy |
| chosen by the locking script | γ, δ, L, and e(α, β) |

The second-to-last row is the soundness property. A spender who could choose γ
could choose one satisfying the equation for a proof of nothing.

## Table 5 — what the network has executed

| | bytes | share of a pairing | status |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Miller loop, complete | 332,977 | 35.6% | **mainnet** |
| `fp12.powX`, one of 5 ladders | 98,902 | 10.6% | **mainnet** |
| final exponentiation, whole | 592,008 | 63.3% | interpreter |
| e(P, Q), whole | 935,334 | 100% | interpreter |

**46.2% of one pairing, by bytes, has been executed by the Bitcoin network.**
The Miller-loop stage is complete; of the final exponentiation, one of its
5 f^|x| ladders is. Shares are taken against the emitted pairing, not
against the sum of its stages, which is smaller.

The default script-size policy is 500,000 bytes, so the final
exponentiation (592,008) and the whole pairing (935,334) cannot be
relayed as single locking scripts. The Miller loop can, and is.
